back: Acid: proton (H⁺) donor. Base: proton acceptor (uses a lone pair).
Two species that differ by one proton, e.g. CH₃COOH/CH₃COO⁻, NH₄⁺/NH₃, H₃O⁺/H₂O.
An acid that is fully dissociated into ions in aqueous solution (HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄).
An acid that is only partially dissociated in water, giving an equilibrium (e.g. ethanoic acid).
Strong/weak: extent of dissociation. Concentrated/dilute: amount of acid per dm³.

front: Comparing 0.1 mol dm⁻³ HCl and CH₃COOH
back: HCl: lower pH, higher conductivity, faster with Mg. Same total H₂ with excess Mg.
Amphoteric: a base with HCl (forms H₃O⁺), an acid with NH₃ (forms OH⁻).
The stronger the acid, the weaker its conjugate base (Cl⁻ is a very weak base).
